evaluations.rationale: Screenplay A faithfully covers many narrative beats from the book and offers clear flashbacks and voiceovers, though its pacing can feel a bit uneven and some dialogue is overly expository.
Screenplay B covers most beats with a natural tone and clear visuals but suffers slightly from a name change (Jake instead of Peter) and a somewhat less engaging overall cinematic execution.
Screenplay C is visually rich and faithful to the source, with strong montage sequences and a wide scope of narrative beats that lend themselves well to AI video clip generation.

Screenplay D achieves a tight, contemporary structure with clearly delineated flashbacks and present-day scenes, strong character descriptions, and natural dialogue that make it highly directable for AI-generated video clips.
Screenplay E retells many of the book’s events but tends to be overly summary and expository, lacking the cinematic details and crisp dialogue necessary for effective short video clip adaptation.

Screenplay F offers the most polished, continuous narrative with clear age and time disambiguation, detailed visual directions, and authentic dialogue that perfectly translate the book’s complex emotional beats into filmable short clips.

judgeSummaryNotes: Strongest: Screenplay F because it delivers an exceptionally clear, cinematic, and coherent adaptation with precise visuals and character continuity; Weakest: Screenplay E because its overly summary style and lack of detailed, directable visual and dialogue cues detract from full production readiness.
